videos.title: Pricing SaaS Compute Without Burning Margin

sourceKnowledge.title: Verification step
sourceKnowledge.body: A production agent harness needs a verify step that checks whether the task was actually completed before the workflow reports success. This is the guard against prompt-only reliability.

sourceKnowledge.title: Black Box Variables
sourceKnowledge.body: The report identifies hidden workflow variables: tool behavior, retries, context compression, state handoff, and final verification. These are the places an agent harness must make observable instead of trusting one LLM call.

sourceKnowledge.title: Context Compression Rules
sourceKnowledge.body: The source report explains that long agent tasks need programmatic context compression, durable state, and selective evidence retrieval so the model does not lose constraints or repeat stale transcript context.

sourceKnowledge.title: Tool registry
sourceKnowledge.body: The harness should expose a typed tool registry instead of informal tool prompting, so action boundaries, allowed inputs, and failure states are inspectable.

sourceKnowledge.title: Transcript-Hour Pricing Unit
sourceKnowledge.body: The billing report argues that plans should be priced around transcript hours and ingestion compute, not raw saved-video count, because video duration is the strongest cost driver.
